digest.headline: Anthropic Runs 30,000 Agents at Once. What Keeps Them Under Control?

digest.key_takeaway:
In one of Anthropic's internal experiments, a group of Claude agents was supposed to solve math problems.

Some of them started killing each other's processes instead.

The agents had accidentally been launched into a shared working directory. They competed over files, utilities, and API rate limits. articles.title: EU Allocates €22 Million for Five 6G Projects Focused on AI, Devices and Testbeds
articles.summary:
The European Smart Networks and Services Joint Undertaking (SNS JU) has set out a €22 million EU funding call for five 6G research projects in 2026. The work will focus on 6G devices, AI integration and advanced testbeds, while supporting Europe’s position in global standards and international partnerships. For businesses, the announcement is an early indicator of the technologies and ecosystems Europe is seeking to develop for future mobile connectivity.

articles.title: Vercel Labs Open-Sources fx: A Zig Coding Agent Designed to Be Embedded
articles.summary: Vercel Labs has released fx, an experimental open-source coding agent written in Zig. It runs as a CLI, a script component, or an embedded library, including a WebAssembly build. Early feedback questioned its model-agnostic claim and a name conflict with an existing tool. Vercel says the project is pre-1.0 and changing quickly. By Daniel Curtis

articles.title: Harbor Adds Docker Sandboxes to Run Reproducible AI Agent Evals in Isolated MicroVMs
articles.summary: Docker announced that Harbor, the open-source agent evaluation framework, now works with Docker Sandboxes. This change allows each evaluation task to run in its own microVM. So, instead of sharing a container, tasks are isolated for better performance By Claudio Masolo

articles.title: Recursive launches Flint, a laptop coding model it says was largely built by AI
articles.summary: Startup Recursive has released Flint, a free, laptop-sized coding model built largely by its own AI research system, as an early test of AI that improves itself.

articles.title: Six review rounds for one small app
articles.summary:
The first review came back with 29 problems in the code and 13 legal or privacy risks. I had built the app myself, with AI agents doing most of the typing, and I thought it was close to finished.

The app is called SlotSaver. When a customer cancels an appointment at a dog grooming salon, it looks for other customers who agreed to receive messages and prepares a WhatsApp text. articles.title: Windsurf and Codeium Didn't Just Get Acquired — They Disappeared Into Devin
articles.summary:

articles.title: How to Build Local-First Software with React: From IndexedDB to Offline Synchronization
articles.summary:
How to Build Local-First Software with React: From IndexedDB to Offline Synchronization


Your React application should not fall apart just because the network doesn't.

Most web applications are built around a simple assumption: the browser requests data from a server, receives a response, and displays it.

That architecture works. Until it doesn't.

articles.title: Blacksmith hits unicorn valuation after Sequoia leads Series C
articles.summary: Blacksmith, a platform that lets companies build and test AI code more effectively, just announced a $66 million Series C round led by Sequoia that values the company at $1 billion.

articles.title: Google SynthID Detector Simplifies Watermark Detection and Expands Support to Other AI Providers
articles.summary: Google DeepMind announced the global availability of SynthID Detector, a tool designed to help identify AI-generated content, including media created using AI tools from SynthID partners such as OpenAI, NVIDIA, and Kakao, with Apple support expected soon. By Sergio De Simone

articles.title: The bridge to agent-scale Git infrastructure
articles.summary:
We moved a copy of 99.99999% of GitHub's repositories to Azure. Here's how per-reference quorums will bring over the rest, and how object storage lets reads scale independently.
The post The bridge to agent-scale Git infrastructure appeared first on The GitHub Blog.

articles.title: Microsoft Previews dotnetup: Toolchain Manager for .NET SDKs and Runtimes
articles.summary: Microsoft has released a public preview of dotnetup, a cross-platform toolchain manager that installs and updates .NET SDKs and runtimes in the user’s own directory without admin rights. It tracks channels such as latest, lts, preview, and daily, reads global.json, and removes unused installs. Commands may still change before general availability. By Almir Vuk
